name: WorkerThreadPool is Godot 4's default off-main-thread tool
summary: The pool exists at startup, so add_task/add_group_task cost nothing like creating a Thread; every task must still be waited for exactly once.
detail: add_task(action, high_priority=false, description="") and add_group_task(action, elements, tasks_needed=-1, high_priority=false, description="") — the group callable is invoked with 0..elements-1. wait_for_task_completion / wait_for_group_task_completion is what frees the task allocation, so it is required even after is_task_completed() returns true; calling it from inside another task can return ERR_BUSY. The docs warn the pool hurts if a task is not computationally expensive (rule of thumb: about a millisecond of real work per task). Godot 4.7's Using multiple threads manual page never mentions this class — the class reference is the only documentation.

name: What is and is not thread-safe in Godot 4
summary: The scene tree is not thread-safe for reads or writes; most servers are; resources may be loaded on threads but not mutated from two; AStar is not.
detail: From the Thread-safe APIs manual page for 4.7: interacting with the active scene tree is not thread-safe — use call_deferred/set_deferred. Building a scene chunk outside the tree on a thread and then add_child.call_deferred() is the sanctioned pattern. Instancing nodes that render is unsafe unless Rendering > Threads > Thread Model is Multi-Threaded, which the same page says has several known bugs. Avoid GPU work off-thread (texture creation, image readback) because it stalls against the RenderingServer. RenderingServer.call_on_render_thread(callable) is the supported way to reach rendering internals.

name: Lock-free fan-out: element writes are thread-safe, resizes are not
summary: GDScript Array and Dictionary element reads and writes are safe across threads; anything that changes the container size is not — so size once, then let N workers write disjoint indices.
detail: This is the single most useful sentence on the Thread-safe APIs page and it removes the mutex from most parallel work: call resize() on the main thread before submitting, then have each add_group_task element write only its own index. append(), resize(), erase() and pop_* from a worker are the bug that reproduces once a week on one machine.

name: Thread, Mutex and Semaphore, and when they beat the pool
summary: A long-lived worker that owns a queue and sleeps on a Semaphore is the one case where Thread beats WorkerThreadPool; the join in _exit_tree is mandatory and Godot's Mutex is reentrant.
detail: A pool task that never returns permanently occupies a worker, so a persistent worker must be a real Thread. There is no cancel: cooperate with a flag under a mutex, post the semaphore to wake it, then wait_to_finish(). A Thread reaching refcount zero while started, holding a mutex, or waiting on a semaphore is a crash. Mutex is reentrant — lock twice, unlock twice — and try_lock() returns true if the caller already owns it, which hides double-lock bugs. Semaphore.post(count=1) can release several waiters; try_wait() is the non-blocking form. The manual warns that creating threads is slow, especially on Windows, and that mutex lock/unlock is itself expensive.

name: call_deferred and set_deferred: the only safe way back to the scene tree
summary: Callable.call_deferred() queues a call that runs during idle time — mainly at the end of process and physics frames — and always returns null, not the method's result.
detail: Modern idiom is method.call_deferred(args) and node.set_deferred(&"property", value); the Godot 3 string form call_deferred("method", args) still works but is unchecked. Deferring a method from itself is infinite recursion, exactly as a direct call would be. Deferred is not 'next frame' — it may flush at the end of the current process frame — so use await get_tree().process_frame when a one-frame delay is what you meant. Ordering is queue order and is not ordered against signals emitted later in the frame.

name: The deferred-call queue is finite and drops calls silently
summary: memory/limits/message_queue/max_size_mb defaults to 32MB; overflow prints "Message queue out of memory" and discards the call rather than crashing.
detail: core/object/message_queue.cpp prints 'Failed method: %s. Message queue out of memory.' and equivalents for deferred sets and notifications. The failure mode is a silently skipped update, which is far harder to diagnose than a crash. Anything that defers once per object per frame across hundreds of objects will reach it: defer one batch, not N items.

name: ResourceLoader threaded loading, and the ways it still blocks
summary: load_threaded_request / load_threaded_get_status / load_threaded_get; get() blocks if the load is unfinished, and status must be polled at most once per process frame.
detail: Signatures: load_threaded_request(path, type_hint="", use_sub_threads=false, cache_mode=CACHE_MODE_REUSE) -> Error; load_threaded_get_status(path, progress: Array = []) -> ThreadLoadStatus; load_threaded_get(path) -> Resource. Status is INVALID_RESOURCE 0, IN_PROGRESS 1, FAILED 2, LOADED 3. CacheMode IGNORE 0, REUSE 1, REPLACE 2, IGNORE_DEEP 3, REPLACE_DEEP 4 — the DEEP variants are 4.3+. use_sub_threads recursively parallelises dependencies and the class reference warns it can cause in-game slowdowns because one load can saturate the shared pool. Loads are submitted to WorkerThreadPool via add_native_task, so they compete with your own tasks. resource_loader.cpp detects the main thread polling the same task twice within one Engine.get_process_frames() value and forces progress ('Support userland polling in a loop on the main thread'), so a busy-wait terminates — while freezing the frame. Prefer change_scene_to_packed() over change_scene_to_file(), which loads synchronously.

name: await, process_frame, and why await is not a thread
summary: await get_tree().process_frame resumes immediately before _process runs next frame; await hides latency on the main thread and never moves work off it.
detail: SceneTree.process_frame is 'emitted immediately before Node._process() is called on every node in this tree', and physics_frame is its physics counterpart — so a coroutine resuming on process_frame runs ahead of the frame's normal work and can be cut short by that frame's budget check. await replaces Godot 3's yield entirely. Do not await on a worker thread: resumption is driven by main-thread signal emission and the engine documents no thread contract for GDScript function state. Awaiting inside _ready() makes the node count as ready the moment the coroutine suspends. Awaiting something that is neither a signal nor a coroutine returns immediately with a runtime warning that static typing will not catch.

name: Slice amortised work by a microsecond deadline, never by item count
summary: Time.get_ticks_usec() plus await get_tree().process_frame gives a budget that degrades gracefully on slow devices; a fixed N-per-frame is a budget in the wrong unit.
detail: Arm a deadline of Time.get_ticks_usec() + budget, do one unit, check, and await process_frame when spent. The check happens after a unit, so the unit must fit inside the budget — a 12ms unit blows a 2ms budget however the loop is written; the fix is to split the unit, not lower the budget. Deadlines compose (two jobs can share one budget object and the total stays bounded) and counts do not. Do this in _process, not _physics_process, because physics can run several times per rendered frame when catching up and silently multiplies the budget.

name: Measure the worst frame, not the average framerate
summary: Engine.get_frames_per_second() is an average and hides the single 40ms frame the player actually feels; use Time.get_ticks_usec() deltas and record the maximum.
detail: get_frames_per_second() is documented as 'the average frames rendered every second'. Time.get_ticks_usec() is monotonic microseconds since engine start on a 64-bit value. Engine.get_process_frames() increments every process frame 'regardless of whether the render loop is enabled', which makes it a reliable once-per-frame guard. A hitch is a distribution tail, so instrument for the tail.

name: The web export has no threads by default, and threading code fails silently there
summary: Since 4.3 the default web build is single-threaded: WorkerThreadPool runs tasks inline inside add_task(), and Thread.start() is compiled to an empty body.
detail: Threaded web builds need SharedArrayBuffer and therefore Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin plus Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp; 4.3 added an 'Ensure Cross-Origin Isolation Headers' export option that injects them via a PWA service worker. On a non-threaded build main.cpp calls WorkerThreadPool::init(0, 0), and worker_thread_pool.cpp's _post_tasks falls back to processing on the calling thread when there are no workers — so add_task() runs the callable to completion before returning, and load_threaded_request() performs the whole load inside the request call. core/os/thread.h compiles start() to {} and is_started() to false without THREADS_ENABLED, so a script-level Thread.start() returns OK, never runs the function, and wait_to_finish() then errors. Guard with OS.has_feature("threads") — 'threads' and 'nothreads' are documented feature tags. Design rule: write the work so it is correct when it runs inline. Related: without threads the web build plays audio as Sample rather than Stream (audio/general/default_playback_type).

name: Shader pipeline compilation is a frame-time cliff your own code cannot fix
summary: The first draw of a material variant compiles a GPU pipeline; ubershaders are 4.4+, the Shader Baker export option is 4.5+ and is not supported on web.
detail: Ubershaders (4.4+) precompile one general pipeline using specialization constants and compile optimised variants in the background during play. The Shader Baker export option (4.5+) bundles compiled shader code into the PCK so the compilation step is skipped entirely — Forward+ and Mobile renderers only, not Compatibility, on Windows (Vulkan/D3D12), macOS (Vulkan/Metal), Linux (Vulkan) and Android (Vulkan), and not on web. The universal fallback is still to render every material once, invisible or off-camera, during loading.

name: Bake Image on a worker, upload ImageTexture on the main thread
summary: Image is CPU-side and safe to build off-thread; ImageTexture is a GPU object whose creation off-thread stalls the RenderingServer — and Image.create() is deprecated in favour of create_empty().
detail: Image.create_empty(width, height, use_mipmaps, format) is the current static constructor; Image.create() is marked deprecated in the 4.7 reference and create_empty does not exist in the 4.2 reference, so it is 4.3+. ImageTexture.create_from_image(image) allocates; set_image() reallocates; update(image) reuses the allocation and requires matching size, format and mipmap configuration, and is documented as faster for frequent updates. Split any procedural sprite bake along that line: pixels in parallel, upload serial.

name: Bake sprites once at max size instead of re-baking per resize
summary: The u+DPR sprite cache key exists to work around Canvas2D; Godot scales textures on the GPU for free, so the whole resize re-bake can be deleted rather than threaded.
problem: buildSprites() re-bakes every gameplay sprite whenever u, DPR, W, H or skyI moves, and the source comment measures the cost at 1-2ms — accepted today only because it lands on the tier-banner frame. artifactSprite() keys its bank on u + ':' + DPR and throws the whole bank away when either moves. Both exist because Canvas2D has no cheap way to draw a shadow-blurred shape at an arbitrary size each frame.
proposal: In the Godot rebuild, bake each sprite once at the largest size the device will ever need and let node transforms scale it down on the GPU. Keep the resize path to the cheap arithmetic only (R, AY, cy, safe-area box). Where a bake genuinely must re-run for a material change, do the Image work as a WorkerThreadPool.add_group_task fan-out and upload with ImageTexture.create_from_image on the main thread.
risk: Baking at max size costs VRAM and can soften small sprites if filtering is wrong; the rim-light rotation trick depends on the baked lit edge, so the bake orientation must survive the change.

name: Pre-warm per-kind sprite bakes from the level table, not on first draw
summary: artifactSprite() bakes lazily on first draw, so the first blinker, mirror orb and black hole of a run each cost a bake in the frame they appear.
problem: artifactSprite(kind) checks artifactBank and bakes the kind on demand, inside the draw pass. The black hole's first appearance is also the frame the arena re-spaces its rings, and a formation's first appearance is a frame the player is being asked to react to. The cost is invisible in aggregate FPS and very visible as a single long frame.
proposal: Walk the level's own data — its formation tiers and orb pool — at level load and pre-warm every kind it can spawn, using an explicit microsecond frame budget with await get_tree().process_frame between units. Nothing should be baked for the first time during a run.
risk: Pre-warming everything a level can spawn raises peak texture memory and level-load time; the level tables must actually enumerate the spawnable set or the warm-up will miss kinds and hide the problem instead of fixing it.

name: Decide the web export's threading posture before writing threaded code
summary: Godot's default web export has no threads, so Thread-based work silently does nothing and pool-based work silently blocks — this has to be a decision, not a discovery.
problem: Cosmo ships to web today and the Godot rebuild is expected to as well. On a default (single-threaded) web export WorkerThreadPool runs tasks inline inside add_task(), ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request() performs the whole load in the request call, and Thread.start() is compiled to an empty body so the worker function never runs at all. Threading code written and tested on desktop will pass every check and behave differently in the shipped web build.
proposal: Adopt three rules for the rebuild: (1) never use Thread where WorkerThreadPool will do, because the pool degrades to synchronous and Thread degrades to nothing; (2) keep every task small enough that running it inline on the main thread is survivable; (3) guard any genuinely long-lived worker with OS.has_feature("threads") and provide the inline path. Decide separately whether the web build ships cross-origin isolated (COOP/COEP, or the 'Ensure Cross-Origin Isolation Headers' PWA option) and record the choice, because it also governs whether audio plays as Stream or Sample.
risk: Cross-origin isolation breaks embedding and third-party requests, which affects the optional cloud account path; choosing no-threads permanently caps what can be moved off the main thread on web.

name: Adopt one microsecond frame-budget helper for all amortised work
summary: Give the rebuild a single FrameBudget object with a microsecond deadline, so every amortised job — pre-warming, loading, migration — degrades the same way on a slow phone.
problem: Cosmo's current long-frame sources are handled ad hoc: the sprite bake is timed by a comment, the per-kind bake is unbudgeted, and nothing measures the worst frame. Engine.get_frames_per_second() is an average and will report 60 through a 40ms hitch. Without a shared budget, each new amortised job invents its own 'N per frame' constant that is wrong on the next device.
proposal: Ship a FrameBudget RefCounted (open(usec) / spent(), on Time.get_ticks_usec()) and require every amortised loop to use it with await get_tree().process_frame, in _process rather than _physics_process. Instrument the worst frame with ticks_usec deltas rather than the FPS average, so a regression check can assert a maximum rather than a mean.
risk: A budget that is too small turns one long frame into many slightly long frames, which can feel worse; the unit of work must fit inside the budget or the helper gives false confidence.

name: Warm the sky ShaderMaterial's pipeline on the title screen
summary: The custom sky's first draw is a GPU pipeline compilation; put it on the title screen deliberately, because Shader Baker does not cover the web export.
problem: Cosmo's sky is one full-screen shader draw and the glow chain is six render targets. In Godot each material variant compiles a pipeline the first time it is actually drawn, which is a stall. If the sky's first draw is the first frame of a run, the stall lands on the frame the player starts playing.
proposal: Draw the sky material once, invisible or off-camera, while the title screen is up — the warm-up the pipeline-compilation page recommends. Enable the Shader Baker export option (4.5+) for the Android build, where it is supported, and accept that the web build must pay the first compile somewhere and should pay it on the title screen. Verify that the eight world morph targets do not each produce a distinct pipeline; if they do, warm them all.
risk: A warm-up draw on the title screen costs title-screen frame time and could be visible if the material is not fully hidden; Shader Baker is reported to lengthen export times substantially.

name: Threaded-load the eight world backdrops from the title screen
summary: The sky changes at ladder milestones — mid-run — so the world textures must already be resident; request them in the background while the title screen is up.
problem: BootScene loads art/manifest.json and queues every valid texture before the game starts, and the runtime resolves a world backdrop through getTexture at the moment the band changes. In Godot the equivalent lazy resolve would be a synchronous load in the middle of a run, at exactly the moment the tier banner and the world change are already competing for the frame. The manifest also declares 34 keys of which only 26 are ever requested.
proposal: Request the eight world backdrops with ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request() when the title screen appears, poll status once per frame, and hold the retrieved textures for the session. Never resolve a world texture on the frame the band changes. Drop the 8 declared-but-unrequested manifest keys rather than porting them.
risk: Holding eight backdrops resident raises peak texture memory on low-end phones; the procedural-fallback contract must still hold if a load fails, so the failure path needs testing rather than assuming.

name: Extend the teardown rule to threads, tasks and in-flight loads
summary: "Reloading must never leave a second game running beside the first" has to cover joined threads, waited-for pool tasks and retrieved load tokens, or the Godot rebuild reintroduces the double-loop bug in a new shape.
problem: Cosmo's scene-shutdown invariant exists because a second live loop once survived a reload. Godot adds three new ways for work to outlive its scene: an unjoined Thread, a WorkerThreadPool task nobody waited for, and a load_threaded_request whose resource was never retrieved. Godot punishes the first with a crash and the other two with leaks, and none of them are visible in a screenshot.
proposal: State the teardown contract for the rebuild as: every long-lived Thread joined in _exit_tree(), every submitted task id waited for exactly once, every issued load request retrieved or abandoned deliberately. Give it a check in the same family as the existing scene-teardown assertion, since this is precisely the class of bug the current harness was written for.
risk: A join in _exit_tree can block shutdown if the worker does not observe its exit flag promptly; the cooperative-cancel protocol has to be right or teardown hangs instead of leaking.
